textTranslated:
Here's a complete review of the Wish Boat.
First, there are two types of Wish Boats: motorboats and ferryboats.
For both, a temporary booth opens at a certain time. Buy yours at the booth, not the touts.
Motorboats are located east of Old City. Groups of 4-6 people pay 180,000 dong, and each person gets a free wish lantern.
Buy a ticket, then go to the appropriate booth at the time you want to ride, present your ticket, and hop on.
Further west than the motorboats (as if heading upwards), all the way up to the bridge (night market), you'll start to see people carrying boats in green vests, and you'll also see the booth. There's usually a line here around sunset, so you can easily recognize them.
For 4-6 people, the price is 220,000 dong, and the wish lanterns are sold separately.
There are many touts selling wish lanterns, but they usually sell one for 10,000 dong. Some older ladies even sell two for 10,000 dong.

Motorboats sail a little farther out, release wish lanterns, and then return.
Ferry boats gather in groups, each offering a unique atmosphere. Motorboats offer a refreshing sense of openness, so both have their own unique charm.
Before sunset, motorboats are the way to go, and after sunset, ferry boats are the way to go.
As an aside, there are a lot of bird-shaped flying toys for sale, but never buy them. They break or break within 20 minutes. And even if you buy one, most people won't be able to fly it well anyway.

textTranslated:
2025/02/18
There are boat landings on both banks of the river.
Tickets are sold at places with tables and signs.
There is one on each bank. The prices are also listed.
For 170,000 VND, you can charter a boat that can accommodate up to 3 people for 20 minutes. One ticket is valid for one or two people.
Candles are an extra charge; a vendor was selling them for 30,000 VND before boarding the boat. The total cost, including the boat ticket, is 200,000 VND (approximately 1,200 yen), and it's a 20-minute experience for 1 to 3 people. The boatman will light the candles with a lighter when you reach a suitable spot.
We boarded at 7:00 PM, but had to wait in line for about 20 minutes beforehand. The boats move quickly, so don't give up even if the line is long. Holding onto the handrail on the pier stairs and crouching down ensures you get a life jacket, making it a safe experience. Depending on the water level, be careful of your head when passing under the bridge ⚠️. The more boats there are, the more beautiful it is. The boatman will take your smartphone and take lots of commemorative photos for you ♪
It was a very enjoyable night cruise.

A beautiful historic house in the heart of Hoi An's Old Town. The Nha Cu Quan Thang is an impressive example of the traditional architecture of this ancient trading city and beautifully showcases the fusion of various Asian cultures. ✨

A wonderful spot for anyone who loves history, culture, and traditional architecture. Not as crowded as other tourist attractions, it's perfect for glimpsing Hoi An's past while strolling through the Old Town.

Quan Thang Ancient House is one of the historically significant old houses in Hoi An's Old Town (77 Trán Phu Street).

Built in the 18th century (or approximately 150-300 years ago), it was the residence of Quan Thang, a merchant from Guangzhou, China. Architecture: Known for its beautiful blend of Chinese and Vietnamese architectural styles, it utilizes precious wood hand-carved by skilled craftsmen. Highlights include the exquisite wood carvings and the courtyard design based on feng shui principles.

textTranslated:
Hoi An, the Land of Lanterns!

I have already visited Hoi An three times, but all were on group tours; this is my first time traveling alone.

Generally, it is easy to think of Hoi An as an outlying area of ​​Da Nang, merely as a brief half-day stopover during a Da Nang tour.

This itinerary was determined due to the difficulties associated with group tours. From a travel agency's perspective, they need an environment where they can easily secure accommodations for a large group and manage meals and transportation smoothly. However, since Hoi An is a UNESCO Historic Area, there are no large hotels or restaurants within the town.

I had planned this trip to Hoi An without much thought, simply following the schedule I had taken on a group tour before. However, it was only after arriving at the destination that I realized I had made a mistake.

For a private trip aimed at sightseeing or relaxation, the conclusion is that a suitable itinerary would be to spend most of the time in Hoi An and then stop by Da Nang for a day or two on the way back home.

That is how advantageous Hoi An is from the perspective of sightseeing and relaxation.

If we consider the advantages of tourism in Da Nang,

First and foremost, it would be Vietnam's affordable prices,

but this cannot be considered a unique advantage of Da Nang.

Next is the fact that it is a fairly modern city situated by the sea; however, compared to the common beach towns in Korea, one might wonder, "Why bother flying all the way here?"

This is because there are only a few tourist spots in Da Nang where one can find the unique atmosphere and culture of Vietnam to be moved by and enjoy a relaxing vacation.

However, things change when you come down to Hoi An.

Just like other world-renowned tourist destinations, the entire city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site,

so unique cultural elements that can only be seen and experienced here are abundant in the surrounding houses, accommodations, and streets.

The lanterns that adorn the entire city—a defining feature of Hoi An—entice travelers with their diverse patterns and colors, displaying a variety of colors and patterns as numerous as the countless shops lining the streets. Sitting in any café in the city adorned with colorful lanterns in the evening, leisurely sipping a beer, and taking in the sight of rowboats carrying lights as beautiful as the city itself is enough to say that the purpose of the tour has been almost fully achieved.

It is the exact same place I visited on a group tour before...???

The only difference from then is that there is no guide here who used to make me stare at my watch the entire time after being told, "We will meet again at the square in 20 minutes"!

When you get tired of the Old Town, you can simply head to the nearby An Bang Beach.

Unlike Da Nang's My Khe Beach, An Bang Beach is nature-friendly and overflows with charming, quaint beauty.

This means that the lush palm trees and surrounding parasols blend exceptionally well with the beach scenery.

If the fun of Da Nang's My Khe Beach lies in gazing at the wide, expansive sandy beach, An Bang Beach naturally makes you feel the urge to cross the shore and jump into the seawater. And even with smartphone photos, you can get better results at An Bang Beach than at My Khe Beach.

This is because An Bang Beach allows you to fully experience an exotic charm, making you feel as if you have come to an island on the equator.
text:
등불의 나라 호이안!

호이안은 벌써 3번이나 다녀 왔지만,
모두 단체관광이였고 개인관광은 이번이 처음이다.

일반적으로 호이안은 다낭의 부속지역으로서 다낭 관광때에 한나절 잠시 다녀오는것으로 생각하기 쉽다.

이러한 코스가 결정된 이유는 단체관광의 어려움 때문이라고 할 수 있다. 여행사의 입장에서 보면,
단체 인원을 숙박시킬 숙소를 쉽게 구할 수가 있고 식사와 이동을 원할하게 운영할 수 있는 환경이 되어야 하는데 이곳 호이안은 유네스코 역사 보존지역이라서 타운내에는 대형호텔도 식당도 없다.

이번 호이안 여행도 별 생각없이 예전에 단체로 와 봤던 일정대로 계획했던 나는,
여행지에 도착해 보고 나서야 잘 못된 생각이였다는 것을 깨달았다.

관광이나 휴양을 목적으로 한 개인의 여행이라면,
대부분의 일정은 호이안에서 지내다가 귀국시에 하루 이틀 다낭에 들렸다가 가는 코스가 적합하다는 결론이다.

그만큼 관광이나 휴양이라는 관점에서는 호이안이 더 유리하다.

다낭 관광의 장점이라면,
우선적으로 베트남의 저렴한 물가가 되겠지만,
이 점은 다낭만의 장점이라고 할수는 없다.

다음으로 바다를 끼고 제법 현대적인 도시의 모습을 갖추고 있다는 점인데,
한국의 흔한 해변 도시와 비교할 때 구태어 비행기를 타고 여기까지?
하는 의문이 들기도 한다.

왜냐하면,
베트남만의 정취나 문화속에서 감동을 받고 휴양도 즐기기 위한 관광적인 요소를 다낭에서 찾으려면 몇 군데 정도에 불과하기 때문이다.

그러나 호이안으로 내려오면 그것이 달라 진다.

세계유수의 이름난 관광지가 그러하듯,
여기도 도시 전체가 유네스코 선정 지역이라서,
반드시 이곳에 와서야 보고 느낄 수 있는 독특한 문화적 요소들이 주변의 가옥이나 숙소, 거리 등에 널려 있을 정도로 흔하다.

호이안의 특징인,
온 도시를 장식하고 있는 등불은 각양각색의 무늬와 색깔을 뽐내면서 여행자들을 유혹하는데,
길거리에 늘어선 수 많은 가게의 수 만큼이나 다양한 색깔과 무늬를 보여준다.

저녁 무렵 오색등으로 치장된 도시의 아무 카페에 앉아 느긋하게 맥주를 마시며,
이 도시처럼 아름다운 불빛을 실은 나룻배를 두눈에 담아보는것만으로도 관광의 목적은 거의 달성하였다고 할수있다.

예전 단체관광에도 와 봤던 똑같은 장소인데. . .???
그때와 다른점은 단 하나! "20분후에 광장에서 다시 모입니다" 라는 안내를 받고, 그 시간내내 시계만 쳐다 보게 했던 가이드가 없다는점 뿐이다!

올드 타운이 실증이 날때면 인근의 안방비치로 놀러가면 된다.

안방비치는 다낭의 미케비치와는 다르게 자연 친화적이며 아기자기한 멋이 넘친다.

textTranslated:
The Hoi An Village Experience is one of the most beautiful activities that takes you away from the hustle and bustle of the old city to enjoy rural life and authentic Vietnamese traditions. Ride the traditional circular bamboo boats (thuyền thúng) piloted by locals. Enjoy the beauty of nature amidst the coconut trees, sailing through tranquil waterways to witness the exciting and fast-paced boat rotations and someone casting traditional fishing nets. The experience is wonderful in the pleasant weather, but it's extremely hot in the summer. We rode in July, and it was incredibly hot. The experience is enjoyable, but I don't recommend it during the midday heat. The hours are from 8 AM to 8 PM, every day. It's very crowded in the morning, so we went in the afternoon when it was less busy. Beware of scammers at the gate. Once inside, you'll find people selling things; try to haggle because they will raise the prices. Initially, a woman asked us for 300,000 VND per person. Approximately 42 Saudi Riyals.

We reduced the price of the boat for 4 people to 600,000 Dong, which is 85 Saudi Riyals.
We bought it without the coconut juice and food because it wouldn't suit us.
There is a restroom (excuse the expression), but it's not clean.
If you found my review helpful, please like it 🤍

This street features a variety of cafes and restaurants housed in repurposed, antique houses.

Hoi An's ancient cultural heritage (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) and the appearance of the ancient city still remain along the street.

textTranslated:
Location and Time of the Event

Location: The stage along the Hoai River or the An Hoi Sculpture Garden area in Hoi An Old Town.

Time: Starting around 7:00 PM every night, attracting a large number of locals and tourists.

Gameplay and Performance: The "Anh Hieu" and "Chi Hieu" (Master and Mistress) are the game's facilitators, singing folk songs and rhymes from Quang Nam province to call out the names of the cards. The "Bai Choi" deck consists of 33 cards with colloquial names such as "Nhat Trum," "Nhi Ngheo," "Tam Mieng," and "Ong Co," divided into different decks: Van, Sach, and Van.

Rules of the Game: Players buy cards and listen to the call. Whoever has a card matching the song and calls out three cards on their card first shouts "Tie" and wins, receiving a prize.

Easily recognizable by its distinctive call-and-response, this place takes place in the evening in the Old Quarter area.

text:
October 15, 2026 Day 3 | Hoi An Old Town by Day 🇻🇳

Our Grab ride from Da Nang took around 45 minutes, cost VND 306,800 (approximately S$17), and was a smooth, traffic-free journey. The moment we arrived, I had a feeling I was going to love this place, not just during the day but also in the evening. Hoi An was so cute and rustic, with a romantic charm of its own. We started with a leisurely stroll, admiring the old yellow-painted houses, charming little boutiques, and beautiful canopies covered in plants and vines. I could have wandered those streets for hours!

🍜 An unexpected food gem: Hoàng Local Foods
We passed so many lovely cafés that I was tempted to stop for coffee and dessert, but we were absolutely starving after our morning at the cat café.

Then we came across Hoàng Local Foods, a simple local eatery near the river. It was empty, and for some reason, I have a soft spot for places like that when I travel. I like supporting small local businesses, and an empty restaurant doesn't automatically mean the food isn't good. In fact, some of my best food experiences have happened this way!

So, we took a chance, and am I glad we did!

The owner, whom we affectionately called Uncle, was friendly and had such a cool, laid-back vibe. He was enjoying a cold beer while cooking our food right in front of us. Every dish came out freshly prepared and straight from the pan, and everything was delicious. We loved it so much that we cleaned our plates!

The best part? We paid just VND 500,000 (approximately S$25) for three drinks and five different dishes. A fantastic meal, wonderful hospitality, and a full stomach. Definitely a 5/5 experience, and one I highly recommend!

🍹 Riverside drinks at Đào Tiên Restaurant
After lunch, we continued exploring and squeezed in a few TikTok videos along the way. (My sisters' idea, not mine! 😂)

We eventually came across Đào Tiên Restaurant, a huge riverside restaurant where we stopped for drinks because we were thirsty. I loved the design: high ceilings and a spacious, open interior that felt almost like a huge cave overlooking the river. The place had a fancy feel, and the staff were friendly. Since we only had drinks, I can't really comment on the food, but we enjoyed our stop. Three drinks and our bill came to VND 460,000 (approximately S$23).

🛍️ Tired feet, TikToks, and shopping for Mama and Papa
We explored a little more and took a long walk in the opposite direction from the Old Town. Of course, we made another TikTok, goofed around, laughed, and complained a little as our feet started getting tired. 😂

Then we found a second-hand shop, and suddenly, nobody was tired anymore! Funny how that works. I treated my sisters to a little shopping and picked up a dress for Mama and a windbreaker for Papa.

Our day in Hoi An was such a memorable one. I loved the charming streets, the unexpected food discovery, the riverside views, and all the little moments in between. But what made it extra special was getting to experience everything with my sisters. ❤️

Sometimes, it's not just about the places you visit, but the people you're with and the memories you make along the way.

Hội An vẫn rất tuyệt vời và là điểm đến đáng để trải nghiệm. Con người thân thiện, cảnh đẹp và không khí rất dễ chịu.

Tuy nhiên, mình có một trải nghiệm không vui tại một điểm chụp ảnh đèn lồng. Phí chụp chỉ 20.000đ/lượt nên mình hoàn toàn sẵn sàng trả. Sau khi thanh toán, mình nhờ chị chủ chụp giúp vài tấm vì trước đó thấy chị hỗ trợ khách nước ngoài rất nhiệt tình và khá chuyên nghiệp.

Nhưng với mình, chị từ chối ngay với thái độ khó chịu và bảo tự nhờ người đi cùng chụp. Khi mình thắc mắc vì sao lại có sự khác biệt trong cách đối xử, chị còn tỏ thái độ gay gắt hơn và nói rằng nếu muốn chị chụp thì phải trả thêm tiền.

20.000đ không phải số tiền lớn, nhưng điều khiến mình thất vọng là cách phục vụ và thái độ đối với khách Việt. Mọi người nên cân nhắc trước khi ghé chụp tại đây. Xung quanh vẫn còn nhiều gian hàng được trang trí đẹp, thân thiện và đáng trải nghiệm hơn. Đừng để một trải nghiệm không vui làm ảnh hưởng đến chuyến đi như mình.

Hoi An is still a wonderful place to visit. The people are friendly, the town is beautiful, and the atmosphere is amazing.

Unfortunately, I had a bad experience at one of the lantern photo spots. The photo fee was only 20,000 VND, which I was happy to pay. After paying, I politely asked the owner to help take a few photos because I had seen her doing the same for foreign visitors.

She immediately refused with a rude attitude and told me to ask my friend instead. When I asked why she treated Vietnamese customers differently, she became even more unfriendly and said I had to pay extra if I wanted her to take the photos.

It’s not about the 20,000 VND—it’s about the attitude. There are many other beautiful photo spots nearby with much friendlier service. I recommend choosing those instead.

text:
I had an awesome evening tonight.
Six of us were collected from our hotel and climbed aboard a little green electric buggy for a 90-minute tour of Hoi An and the surrounding countryside.
What followed was one of the most enjoyable excursions of the trip.
We rolled through rice paddies glowing in the last light of the day, spotted water buffalo enjoying an evening swim, passed quiet village roads and local fishing areas, and watched the countryside gradually give way to the lantern-lit magic of Hoi An after dark.
The beauty of travelling by buggy is the pace. Slow enough to actually see everything, fast enough that nobody had to walk kilometres in tropical humidity while pretending they were enjoying it.
The transition from sunset to evening was spectacular. One minute we were watching the last orange glow over the paddies, the next we were cruising beside the river surrounded by lantern boats and colourful reflections dancing on the water.
For a group of foodies and sightseers ranging from enthusiastic to slightly creaky, it was pretty much perfect.
Comfortable. Relaxed. Interesting.
No hard sell. No souvenir shop ambush. No timetable stress.
Just a genuinely lovely evening seeing a different side of Hoi An before being dropped directly at our restaurant at 7.30pm for dinner.
Special mention to the water buffalo, who looked completely unimpressed by six tourists taking photographs while he enjoyed a perfectly peaceful evening swim.
Sometimes the simplest ideas turn out to be the best ones.

text:
This morning I escaped the lantern crowds and spent a few hours wandering around Hoi An in daylight.
I'm glad I did.
Most visitors see Hoi An at night, when the river is glowing, the lanterns are lit and every second person seems determined to recreate the same Instagram photo. It's beautiful, but daytime Hoi An has a completely different personality.
The old town slows down.
The yellow heritage buildings seem richer in colour, the temples are quieter, and the river becomes the star of the show rather than the backdrop. You notice details you miss in the evening – weathered doorways, tiny courtyards, old wooden shutters, bicycles leaning against walls and locals simply getting on with their day.
One of the best things about Hoi An is that there are no rules about how to explore it. Hire a bicycle and meander along the riverfront. Take a traditional boat ride. Stop for a Vietnamese coffee when the mood strikes. Browse a tailor shop. Wander through a market. Sit by the water and watch the world go by for half an hour.
Then get up and do something completely different.
There doesn't need to be a plan.
Some places are about ticking attractions off a list. Hoi An is about slowing down enough to enjoy where you are. Every corner seems to reveal another beautiful building, another hidden lane, another riverside view worth stopping for.
As a foodie, I came for the restaurants. As a traveller, I found myself equally captivated by the town itself.
A few hours spent wandering with no destination, no schedule and no particular purpose turned out to be one of my favourite parts of Hoi An.
Sometimes the best sightseeing is simply allowing yourself to get pleasantly lost.

I absolutely loved my visit to Hoi An Night Market. This place has a unique atmosphere that you cannot find anywhere else. It is a wonderful blend of traditional charm and modern energy. I especially enjoyed the beautiful lanterns, the lively streets, and the cozy riverside setting.

The local food was delicious and reasonably priced, with plenty of options to choose from. There were also many clothing and souvenir shops, making it a great place to explore and shop.

I would highly recommend spending a whole day in Hoi An, from morning until evening, to fully experience the local culture, cuisine, and stunning scenery. If you are visiting central Vietnam, Hoi An Night Market is definitely a place you should not miss.

I would love to come back and visit again in the future.

textTranslated:
Hoi An Night Market Experience

I visited Hoi An Night Market for the first time in the evening and was very impressed. As the sun was setting, the streets began to light up with colorful lanterns. The atmosphere around the old town was filled with warmth, beauty, and unique charm. On both sides of the road, there were many shops selling food, souvenirs, clothes, bags, and traditional crafts. My favorite was the beautifully shaped and colorful lanterns hanging along the shops and streets. The light of the lanterns reflected on the river, making the scenery beautiful and memorable. I walked slowly to enjoy the atmosphere and watch the people walking and playing happily. Along the way, I tried many Vietnamese dishes such as steamed buns, snacks, and local desserts. The food tastes fresh, fragrant and full of flavor. In addition to shopping, I also watched a performance of local music and art. The soft music mixed with the light of the lanterns made the night romantic and warm. I felt that time passed slowly here, allowing me to take a break from the hustle and bustle and soak up the beauty of the old town. Before returning to the hotel, I bought some small souvenirs and took photos to keep as memories. This experience made me love Hoi An even more and want to visit again in the future.

ຕອນ ແລງ ຂ້ອຍ ໄດ້ ມາ ທ່ຽວ ຊົມ ຕະຫຼາດ ກາງ ຄືນ ຮອຍອັນ ເປັນ ຄັ້ງ ທຳອິດ ແລະ ຮູ້ສຶກ ປະທັບໃຈ ຢ່າງ ຫຼາຍ. ເມື່ອ ຕາເວັນ ກຳລັງ ລັບ ຂອບ ຟ້າ ຖະໜົນ ເລີ່ມ ສະຫວ່າງ ດ້ວຍ ແສງ ໂຄມໄຟ ຫຼາຍ ສີ. ບັນຍາກາດ ຮອບ ເມືອງ ເກົ່າ ເຕັມໄປ ດ້ວຍ ຄວາມ ອົບອຸ່ນ ຄວາມ ສວຍງາມ ແລະ ສະເໜ່ ທີ່ ເປັນ ເອກະລັກ. ສອງ ຂ້າງ ທາງ ມີ ຮ້ານ ຂາຍ ອາຫານ ຂອງທີ່ລະນຶກ ເສື້ອຜ້າ ກະເປົາ ແລະ ຫັດຖະກຳ ພື້ນເມືອງ ຫຼາຍ ຊະນິດ. ຂ້ອຍ ມັກ ທີ່ສຸດ ແມ່ນ ໂຄມໄຟ ຮູບຮ່າງ ສວຍງາມ ສີສັນ ອ່ອນໂຍນ ທີ່ ຫ້ອຍ ຢູ່ ຕາມ ຮ້ານ ແລະ ຖະໜົນ. ແສງ ໂຄມໄຟ ສະທ້ອນ ລົງ ເທິງ ແມ່ນ້ຳ ເຮັດໃຫ້ ທິວທັດ ງົດງາມ ແລະ ນ່າຈື່ຈຳ. ຂ້ອຍ ຍ່າງ ໄປ ຢ່າງ ຊ້າໆ ເພື່ອ ຊົມ ບັນຍາກາດ ແລະ ເບິ່ງ ຜູ້ຄົນ ທີ່ ກຳລັງ ຍ່າງ ຫຼິ້ນ ຢ່າງ ມ່ວນຊື່ນ. ລະຫວ່າງ ທາງ ຂ້ອຍ ໄດ້ ລອງ ຊິມ ອາຫານ ຫວຽດນາມ ຫຼາຍ ຢ່າງ ເຊັ່ນ ເຂົ້າຈີ່ ເຝີ ບັ້ນ ອາຫານຫວ່າງ ແລະ ຂອງຫວານ ທ້ອງຖິ່ນ. ລົດຊາດ ອາຫານ ສົດໃໝ່ ຫອມຫວນ ແລະ ມີ ຄວາມ ເຂັ້ມຂົ້ນ ພໍດີ. ນອກຈາກ ການ ຊື້ ຂອງ ແລ້ວ ຂ້ອຍ ຍັງ ໄດ້ ເບິ່ງ ການ ສະແດງ ດົນຕີ ແລະ ສິລະປະ ພື້ນບ້ານ. ສຽງ ດົນຕີ ອ່ອນໂຍນ ປະສົມ ກັບ ແສງ ໂຄມໄຟ ເຮັດໃຫ້ ຄືນນີ້ ມີ ບັນຍາກາດ ໂຣແມນຕິກ ແລະ ອົບອຸ່ນ. ຂ້ອຍ ຮູ້ສຶກ ວ່າ ເວລາ ຢູ່ ບ່ອນນີ້ ໄຫຼໄປ ຢ່າງ ຊ້າໆ ເຮັດໃຫ້ ສາມາດ ພັກ ຈາກ ຄວາມ ວຸ້ນວາຍ ແລະ ດື່ມດ່ຳ ຄວາມງາມ ຂອງ ເມືອງ ເກົ່າ. ກ່ອນ ກັບ ທີ່ພັກ ຂ້ອຍ ໄດ້ ຊື້ ຂອງຝາກ ນ້ອຍໆ ແລະ ຖ່າຍຮູບ ເກັບໄວ້ ເປັນ ຄວາມຊົງຈຳ. ປະສົບການ ຄືນນີ້ ເຮັດໃຫ້ ຂ້ອຍ ຮັກ ຮອຍອັນ ຫຼາຍຂຶ້ນ ແລະ ຢາກ ກັບມາ ຢ້ຽມຢາມ ອີກ ໃນ ອະນາຄົດ.

A magical experience in beautiful Hoi An

Hoi An was absolutely amazing — beautiful, charming and full of magic. Walking through the ancient streets, especially in the evening, felt like stepping into another world. The colourful lanterns, historic buildings and peaceful atmosphere made the whole town feel incredibly special.

The night market was a real highlight. It was lively and colourful, but surprisingly relaxed and easy to enjoy. Unlike many markets, the vendors weren’t overly pushy, which made it much more pleasant to browse, take in the atmosphere and look at the local food, souvenirs and handmade items at our own pace.

The lanterns glowing along the streets and the reflections on the river created such a beautiful and unforgettable scene. Hoi An has a wonderful balance of energy and tranquillity, making it a truly magical place to visit.

We absolutely loved our time there and would happily return.

textTranslated:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Hoi An at night – a magical sea of ​​lights straight out of a fairytale! 🏮✨❤️

WOW! What an incredibly beautiful place! Hoi An completely enchanted us and is one of the most magical places we experienced in Vietnam!

We visited the beautiful old town in the evening, and we highly recommend doing the same!

As soon as the sun sets and the countless colorful lanterns begin to glow, Hoi An transforms into a world that is almost impossible to describe in words.

It truly feels like walking right through a fairytale! ✨

Beautiful, colorful lanterns hang everywhere. The historic houses glow with a warm light, the narrow streets are incredibly romantic, and the many colorful lights are reflected on the river.

The illuminated boats on the water, in particular, create an atmosphere that is simply unforgettable. You'll want to freeze time and hold onto this moment forever.

What particularly captivated us was the combination of the stunning architecture, the charming alleyways, the lovingly decorated shops, and this unique, almost magical atmosphere.

You discover something new around every corner: beautiful lanterns, small cafes, restaurants, charming shops, and countless dreamy photo opportunities.

Our absolute tip: Be sure to visit Hoi An in the evening! 🏮

Only when the many lanterns are lit does the old town truly reveal its magic. Take your time, stroll leisurely through the alleys, walk along the river, and soak up this incredible atmosphere.

Of course, Hoi An is very popular and lively at night. But even with many visitors, this place retains something incredibly special.

We've traveled extensively and seen numerous beautiful places, but Hoi An in the evening is truly something you should experience at least once in your life!

It's romantic, fascinating, colorful, vibrant, and so incredibly beautiful that you'll be constantly amazed.

❤️ Our verdict: An absolute dream!

Hoi An isn't just a beautiful old town. It's an experience brimming with color, light, emotion, and unforgettable impressions.

A place where you truly feel like you're in another world for a few hours.

For us, one of the absolute highlights of our Vietnam trip!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Five stars aren't nearly enough for this fairytale place! We would come back in a heartbeat! ❤️🏮✨
text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Hoi An bei Nacht – ein magisches Lichtermeer wie aus einem Märchen! 🏮✨❤️

WOW! Was für ein unglaublich wunderschöner Ort! Hoi An hat uns absolut verzaubert und gehört für uns zu den magischsten Orten, die wir in Vietnam erlebt haben!

Wir haben die wunderschöne Altstadt am Abend besucht, und genau das können wir jedem nur ans Herz legen!

Sobald die Sonne untergeht und die unzähligen bunten Lampions zu leuchten beginnen, verwandelt sich Hoi An in eine Welt, die man kaum mit Worten beschreiben kann.

Es fühlt sich tatsächlich an, als würde man mitten durch ein Märchen spazieren! ✨

Überall hängen wunderschöne, farbenfrohe Laternen. Die historischen Häuser erstrahlen in warmem Licht, die kleinen Gassen wirken unglaublich romantisch und auf dem Fluss spiegeln sich die vielen bunten Lichter.

Besonders die beleuchteten Boote auf dem Wasser schaffen eine Atmosphäre, die einfach unvergesslich ist. Man möchte am liebsten die Zeit anhalten und diesen Moment für immer festhalten.

Was uns besonders begeistert hat, ist die Kombination aus der wunderschönen Architektur, den gemütlichen Gassen, den liebevoll dekorierten Geschäften und dieser einzigartigen, fast schon magischen Stimmung.

Man entdeckt an jeder Ecke etwas Neues. Wunderschöne Lampions, kleine Cafés, Restaurants, charmante Läden und unzählige traumhafte Fotomotive.

Unser absoluter Tipp: Besucht Hoi An unbedingt am Abend! 🏮

Erst wenn die vielen Laternen leuchten, entfaltet die Altstadt für uns ihren ganzen Zauber. Nehmt euch genügend Zeit, schlendert gemütlich durch die Gassen, spaziert am Fluss entlang und geniesst diese unglaubliche Atmosphäre.

Natürlich ist Hoi An bei Nacht sehr beliebt und entsprechend belebt. Aber selbst mit vielen Besuchern hat dieser Ort etwas unglaublich Besonderes.

Wir sind schon viel gereist und haben zahlreiche wunderschöne Orte gesehen, aber Hoi An am Abend ist wirklich etwas, das man mindestens einmal im Leben erlebt haben sollte!

Es ist romantisch, faszinierend, farbenfroh, lebendig und gleichzeitig so wunderschön, dass man aus dem Staunen kaum herauskommt.

❤️ Unser Fazit: Ein absoluter Traum!

Hoi An ist nicht einfach nur eine schöne Altstadt. Es ist ein Erlebnis voller Farben, Lichter, Emotionen und unvergesslicher Eindrücke.

Ein Ort, an dem man sich für ein paar Stunden tatsächlich wie in einer anderen Welt fühlt.

Für uns eines der absoluten Highlights unserer Vietnamreise!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Fünf Sterne sind für diesen märchenhaften Ort eigentlich viel zu wenig! Wir würden jederzeit wiederkommen! ❤️🏮✨

text: I booked a minubus on klook which dropped me in Hoi an at around 1230 pm. I took a quick lunch at nearby Banh mi phuong restaurant. I ate a Banh mi. Then I bought a ticket for 150 T dong at a roadside kiosk which gave entrance to 5 attractions in the ancient city. I visited the merchant house,fisherman temple,japanese doll exhibition and strolled through the alleys. At one place I enjoyed a draft beer and passed  time till sunset. After sunset I went to the riverside and sat down on a bench to enjoy the memorable view and the decorated boats were floating in the river. People were floating small lanterns in the water. I purchased a 3d ship greeting card,ginger candy and peanuts from local vending women on the riverside.At 8 pm I left. On my way back I enjoyed a vanila croissant at a Takiyaki shop. I was picked up by the cab and dropped at my hotel in Da nang at around 9 pm. Thus ended my second day in Da nang.

textTranslated:
Hoi An Ancient Town Review

📍 Hoi An Ancient Town is one of Vietnam's most famous tourist destinations, recognized by UNESCO as a World Cultural Heritage site in 1999.

🏮 Scenery

* Ancient houses hundreds of years old with architecture blending Vietnamese, Chinese, and Japanese styles.

* Small streets decorated with thousands of vibrant lanterns.

* The romantic Hoai River creates a characteristic Hoi An landscape.

📸 Highlights

* Stroll through the ancient town and take photos with its distinctive yellow walls.

* Visit the Japanese Bridge – the symbol of Hoi An.

* Release floating lanterns on the Hoai River in the evening.

* Enjoy local specialties such as Cao Lau noodles, Quang noodles, Hoi An bread, and chicken rice.

* Explore cafes on elevated platforms to enjoy panoramic views of the ancient town.

🌙 Evening

* This is the most beautiful time to visit.

* Lanterns illuminate the streets, creating a shimmering, ancient atmosphere.

* On the night of the full moon (lunar calendar), many areas dim their lights to recreate the scene of the old town.

👍 Advantages

* Ancient architecture is very well preserved.

* Many cultural activities, local food, and experiences.

* Suitable for families, couples, and photography enthusiasts.

👎 Disadvantages

* Quite crowded on weekends and during peak season.

* Some services are more expensive than in neighboring areas.

* The weather can be quite hot during the day.

💡 Tips

* It's best to visit between 4 PM and 9 PM to enjoy both the daytime view of the old town and the shimmering nighttime atmosphere.

* Purchase entrance tickets if you want to visit the old houses, assembly halls, and museums.

* Combine this with a visit to the Seven-Acre Coconut Forest or An Bang Beach.

⭐ Rating

9.5/10 – One of the most beautiful ancient cities in Southeast Asia, nổi with its ancient architecture, unique culture, and romantic lantern-lit atmosphere. It's an almost unmissable destination when traveling in Central Vietnam. 🏮✨
text:
Review Phố Cổ Hội An

📍 Phố cổ Hội An là một trong những điểm du lịch nổi tiếng nhất Việt Nam, được UNESCO công nhận là Di sản Văn hóa Thế giới năm 1999.

🏮 Cảnh quan

* Những ngôi nhà cổ hàng trăm năm tuổi với kiến trúc giao thoa Việt Nam, Trung Hoa và Nhật Bản.
* Các con phố nhỏ được trang trí bằng hàng nghìn chiếc đèn lồng rực rỡ.
* Dòng sông Hoài thơ mộng tạo nên khung cảnh đặc trưng của Hội An.

📸 Trải nghiệm nổi bật

* Dạo bộ ngắm phố cổ và chụp ảnh với những bức tường vàng đặc trưng.
* Tham quan Chùa Cầu – biểu tượng của Hội An.
* Thả hoa đăng trên sông Hoài vào buổi tối.
* Thưởng thức các món đặc sản như cao lầu, mì Quảng, bánh mì Hội An, cơm gà.
* Khám phá các quán cà phê trên cao để ngắm toàn cảnh phố cổ.

🌙 Buổi tối

* Đây là thời điểm đẹp nhất để tham quan.
* Đèn lồng thắp sáng khắp các tuyến phố tạo nên không gian lung linh, cổ kính.
* Vào đêm rằm âm lịch, nhiều khu vực tắt bớt đèn điện để tái hiện khung cảnh phố cổ xưa.

👍 Ưu điểm

* Kiến trúc cổ được bảo tồn rất tốt.
* Nhiều hoạt động văn hóa, ẩm thực và trải nghiệm địa phương.
* Thích hợp cho cả gia đình, cặp đôi và người yêu nhiếp ảnh.

👎 Nhược điểm

* Khá đông khách vào cuối tuần và mùa cao điểm.
* Một số dịch vụ có giá cao hơn so với khu vực lân cận.
* Ban ngày thời tiết có thể khá nóng.

💡 Kinh nghiệm

* Nên đến từ 16h–21h để vừa ngắm phố cổ ban ngày vừa tận hưởng không khí lung linh về đêm.
* Mua vé tham quan nếu muốn vào các nhà cổ, hội quán và bảo tàng.
* Kết hợp tham quan Rừng Dừa Bảy Mẫu hoặc biển Biển An Bàng.

⭐ Đánh giá

9,5/10 – Một trong những đô thị cổ đẹp nhất Đông Nam Á, nổi bật với kiến trúc cổ kính, văn hóa đặc sắc và không gian đèn lồng lãng mạn. Đây là điểm đến gần như không thể bỏ qua khi du lịch miền Trung Việt Nam. 🏮✨

textTranslated:
For travelers, Hoi An Ancient Town is not just a historical site, but a space of tranquil emotions. The characteristic yellow walls, stained with the passage of time, combined with the green of bougainvillea vines casting shadows on the verandas, create an incredibly subtle and visually stunning color combination.

As the sun sets, Hoi An is bathed in the shimmering beauty of thousands of handcrafted lanterns, reflecting their light onto the romantic Hoai River. Strolling through the narrow streets, enjoying a refreshing herbal drink, or quietly watching the floating lanterns drift on the water is a wonderful way to find balance in your soul. This is not just a tourist destination, but a place to slow down, breathe in the subtle scent of incense, and appreciate the simple yet profound traditional culture of Vietnam. This space will surely provide you with the most creative inspiration and peace.
text:
Phố cổ Hội An trong mắt kẻ lữ hành không chỉ là một di tích, mà là một không gian của những cảm xúc tĩnh tại. Từng mảng tường vàng đặc trưng nhuốm màu thời gian, kết hợp với sắc xanh của giàn hoa giấy rủ bóng bên hiên nhà, tạo nên một sự phối hợp màu sắc vô cùng tinh tế và mãn nhãn.
Khi ánh hoàng hôn dần buông, Hội An khoác lên mình vẻ đẹp lung linh của hàng ngàn chiếc đèn lồng thủ công, phản chiếu ánh sáng xuống dòng sông Hoài thơ mộng. Dạo bước qua những con phố nhỏ, thưởng thức một ly nước mót thảo mộc thanh mát hay ngồi lặng ngắm nhìn những chiếc hoa đăng trôi lững lờ trên mặt nước là cách tuyệt vời để bạn tìm lại sự cân bằng trong tâm hồn. Đây không chỉ là điểm đến để tham quan, mà là nơi để chúng ta chậm lại một nhịp, hít hà mùi trầm hương phảng phất và tận hưởng nét văn hóa truyền thống bình dị nhưng đầy chiều sâu của Việt Nam. Chắc chắn không gian này sẽ mang lại cho bạn những nguồn cảm hứng sáng tạo và bình yên nhất.
